# TracEconomics

> An open tracker of the economy, built only on public data. It computes figures that official statistics don't publish, from the statistics offices' and Eurostat's own files, and publishes the method, the code and every number as open data (CC BY 4.0). Our figures are our own calculations, not official statistics.

Live today: **inflation by household group, for Greece**: how much consumer prices rose for poorer and richer households, renters and owners, household types (one adult, couples, households with children) and pensioner households, month by month, from ELSTAT's and Eurostat's price indices and ELSTAT's Household Budget Survey. Updated each month after ELSTAT publishes the consumer price index. Also live: **consistency of official figures, for Greece**: whether each official figure follows from the inputs the same office publishes (the CPI's rates against its own index, the CPI and HICP rebuilt from their items, household types in the spending survey), how often they agree, and why they differ where they do. More topics and countries will follow.

Every page is also in Greek: replace `/en/` with `/el/` in its address.

Prefer the data files over the pages for numbers: they hold every value at full precision, with the options each one was computed under. The pages state the same numbers in plain words, with the method behind them.

## Inflation by household group: Greece

- [Overview](https://traceconomics.com/en/gr/inflation-by-group/): the latest figures, and how far prices rose for the poorest and the richest fifth of households
- [Explore](https://traceconomics.com/en/gr/inflation-by-group/explore/): every group's index and annual rate, month by month, under each setting of the options
- [Who the groups are](https://traceconomics.com/en/gr/inflation-by-group/groups/): income fifths, household types, renters and owners, pensioner households
- [How it is measured](https://traceconomics.com/en/gr/inflation-by-group/method/): the method, each option, its default and why
- [Calculator](https://traceconomics.com/en/gr/inflation-by-group/calculator/): inflation for a household's own spending pattern

## Consistency of official figures: Greece

- [Overview](https://traceconomics.com/en/gr/official-figures-consistency/): why official figures should add up, how many checks and figures, and how many agree
- [Method](https://traceconomics.com/en/gr/official-figures-consistency/method/): how each check works, what "agree" means, and what a check can tell you
- [Checks](https://traceconomics.com/en/gr/official-figures-consistency/checks/): every check as a plain question with where it stands; each check's page gives its differences with their causes
- [Same question, different sources](https://traceconomics.com/en/gr/official-figures-consistency/same-question/): one question answered by several official sources, with their definitions

## Data

- [Data for Greece](https://traceconomics.com/en/data/gr/): every file, what it holds, its licence and sources
- [How the files are laid out](https://traceconomics.com/en/data/): `/data/v1/{country}/{topic}/latest/`; `latest` always holds the current release
- [Annual and monthly rates, default setting (CSV)](https://traceconomics.com/data/v1/gr/m1/latest/downloads/purchases_excluded_cpi_N_priced/m1_rates.csv): one row per group, measure and month, for all spending (`coicop18` = `TOTAL`). `unit` is the measure: `RCH_A` the annual rate in percent, `RCH_M` the monthly rate, `RCH_A_AVG` the annual-average rate, `RCH_A_GAP` the poorest fifth's annual rate minus the richest fifth's, in percentage points. Groups: income fifths `Q1` (poorest) to `Q5` under `grouping` `B` (the default: people, by equivalised income), `A` (households, by total income) or `C` (people, by equivalised spending); `tenure`; `hhtype` (Eurostat's household types: `A1`, `A2`, `A_GE3` for one, two, three or more adults, `_DCH` with dependent children); `pensioners`. `quality` flags values to read with care.
- [Index, default setting (CSV)](https://traceconomics.com/data/v1/gr/m1/latest/downloads/purchases_excluded_cpi_N_priced/m1_index.csv): each group's price index, 2025 = 100
- [Metadata](https://traceconomics.com/data/v1/gr/m1/latest/metadata.json): the tables, their columns and units, the default options, the period covered, sources, licence and the attribution to keep
- [Settings](https://traceconomics.com/data/v1/gr/m1/latest/settings.json): every combination of the options and its folder under `downloads/`
- [Income limits](https://traceconomics.com/data/v1/gr/m1/latest/income-limits.json): each income fifth's upper limit in euros a year per adult equivalent, ours from the household budget survey (`ours`, every survey year under `years`, with standard errors) and Eurostat's from EU-SILC (`eurostat`), each with its survey and income year
- [Checksums](https://traceconomics.com/data/v1/gr/m1/latest/SHA256SUMS)
- [Consistency checks](https://traceconomics.com/data/v1/gr/m5/latest/checks.json): every check of an official figure against its own inputs: what is compared, how many periods agree, and each difference with its cause (`rounding`, `revision`, `rebasing`, `splice`, `definition` or `not-known`); each check's periods as CSV under `downloads/`
- [Bibliography](https://traceconomics.com/data/v1/references.json): every source the method and pages cite

## Attribution

Credit TracEconomics and keep the notice in each dataset's `metadata.json`. The source data are ELSTAT's (Hellenic Statistical Authority, [www.statistics.gr](https://www.statistics.gr/en/home)) and [Eurostat](https://ec.europa.eu/eurostat)'s; they bear no responsibility for our calculations.
